REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Atomic Energy on
the recommendations contained in the Two Hundred and Ninety-ninth Report of the Department-related
Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and Technology, Environment and Forests on the Demands
for Grants (2017-18) of the Department of Atomic Energy, which was presented to both the Houses of
Parliament on 31st March, 2017. The Committee had in all made thirty seven recommendations/observations
in the report. Action Taken Notes on the report was received by the Committee on 14th August and
4th December, 2017.
The Committee's recommendations, action taken thereon and comments of the Committee on the
Action Taken by the Department of Atomic Energy are set out in the following paragraphs:–
Recommendation
The Committee notes with satisfaction the achievements of the Department of Atomic Energy in its
62 years of operation. In addition to its considerable achievements in the nuclear power generation, the
Department has also produced useful spin-off applications for the benefit of the society and industry.
Keeping in view the Department's success, the Committee is confident that the Department will be able
to fulfil Ten Point Vision outlined by NITI Aayog for the Department. (Para 3.7)
Action Taken
The Department accepts the observations of the Honourable Committee. The Department is working
towards fulfilling the Ten Point Vision outlined by NITI Aayog.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
PERFORMANCE IN THE XII FIVE YEAR PLAN
Physical performance in XII Five Year Plan
Recommendation
The Committee feels that this phenomenon of underutilization of allocated outlay is a very serious
matter towards which the Department needs to focus its attention in a more professional manner and
initiate concrete measures. Merely, reiterating that the Department has already in place a robust monitoring
mechanism would not do any good particularly in view of the fact that underutilization of allocated
budgetary resources has turned out to be a recurring phenomenon. It becomes all the more imperative,
as underutilization of allocated resources provides the Ministry of Finance with an alibi to make less
allocation in the next year and also allows them to use it as a tool to reduce the approved BE outlay
at the RE Stage.
The Committee is of the considered view that the Department can justify its demand for additional
resources only when it is able to first utilise the entire resources allocated to it. The Committee, therefore,

2
recommends that the Department of Atomic Energy must make sincere efforts by way of meticulous
planning, timely implementation and stricter monitoring of schemes/projects. (Para 7.8 and 7.9)
Action Taken
The recommendation of the Committee has been brought to the notice of Heads of Constituent Units
in the Department for meticulous planning and reporting through D.O. letter dated 18.5.2017 for timely
implementation and monitoring.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and would like the Department to constantly monitor the
utilisation of funds.
Recommendation
The Committee also notes that the Department could not get allocations as per the ratio of outlay
approved for the XII Five Year Plan. If the total approved outlay of ` 107186.73 crore for the entire
XII Plan period be evenly distributed among the five Annual Plans, the average allocation comes to
approximately ` 21437.34 crore per Annual Plan. The Committee finds that for 2016-17, the last year
of the Plan period, the plan allocation at BE level was less by ` 5675.46 crore compared to average
allocation per year and if it is seen in the perspective of the RE allocation, this gap further widens to
` 11318.50 crore which is almost the half of the annual allocation during the XII Plan period. The
Committee is aghast to find that for past five years, allocations for Externally Approved Projects could
not be finalised by NITI Aayog/Ministry of Finance. The Committee taking a serious view in this matter
feels that by doing this, Ministry of Finance has made a mockery of approved outlay for the XII Plan
period. (Para 7.10)
Action Taken
The recommendation of the Committee has been brought to the notice of Ministry of Finance for
their kind consideration.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation
The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry of Finance must desist from such practices
and allocate budgetary resources in the Annual Plans in proportion due to the Department or else the
very purpose of long term allocations gets defeated. (Para 7.11)
Action Taken
The recommendation of the Committee has been brought to the notice of Ministry of Finance for
their kind consideration.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply and would like the Department to pursue the matter
with Ministry of Finance for full disbursement of the allocations made.

3
UTILISATION OF THE APPROVED OUTLAY IN 2016-17.
Recommendation
On the overall analysis, the Committee finds that though non-scheme expenditure by the Department
is satisfactory but there is a considerable scope for improvement in the Schemes because actual utilisation
of funds in non-schemes is merely 56% by January, 2017. The Committee, therefore is of the considered
view that Department needs to improve its fund utilisation. (Para 8.5)
Action Taken
Apart from monitoring at Unit level/Department level, monitoring of the Scheme at micro level has
been introduced. The micro-level monitoring is likely to increase the capacity of utilisation of the
allocation. This has enabled nearly 98% utilisation of the overall budget for the year 2016-17.
Comments
The Committee appreciates the monitoring at micro-level and hopes that micro-level
monitoring will improve fund utilisation in non-schemes also.
FUND UTILISATION UNDER INDUSTRIES AND MINERALS SECTOR
Recommendation
The Committee is disappointed to note the financial performance of the Department under Industries
and Minerals Sector and hopes that fund utilisation will see considerable improvement in coming years.
The Committee would like the Department to work proactively to get clearances under projects in
Industries and Minerals Sector. (Para 8.10)
Action Taken
The observations of the Committee are duly noted.
Comments
The Committee while taking note of the reply also expects the Department to give the
details of the action plan chalked out to improve the performance of Industries and Minerals
Sector instead of simply noting it.
Recommendation
The Committee also is of the view that the DAE, being a technologically superior and strategic
Department, should not be put at par with other Departments/Ministries. The Committee finds that in
many cases, progress of schemes/projects depends upon importing equipment from foreign countries,
complex construction requires stage-wise approval which can take time, the Department should also not
be put under the restrictions like Instrument of Service Rule for relocation of budget from one Head to
other Head as equipments involved in nuclear activities may be costlier than 
` 2.5 crore However, the
Department must also desist from underutilising or surrendering funds without any solid reasoning.
(Para 8.12)

4
Action Taken
The observations of the Committee are duly noted.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and would like the Department to constantly monitor the
utilisation of funds.
Recommendation
The Committee, therefore, is of the view that it will be in the fitness of things if the Department
is given a bit more financial flexibility in its financial scheme of things so as to enable it to carry out
its mandate smoothly and efficiently. Ministry of Finance/PMO/Cabinet Committee should also consider
the request of the Scientific Departments to give them desired flexibility in auditing so that scientific
advancement of the country does not get arrested. Cabinet Committee should also consider the proposal
of Scientific Departments for allowing flexibility in auditing favourably. (Para 8.14)
Action Taken
The recommendation of the Committee has been brought to the notice of Ministry of Finance for
their kind consideration.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply but would also like the Department to pursue the
matter with the Ministry of Finance.
BUDGETARY ALLOCATION IN 2017-18
Recommendation
The Committee feels that reduction at approval stage of B.E. to the tune of 
` 8614.00 crore against
the proposed amount of ` 27056.00 crore under BE 2016-17 is unjustified. It has adversely impacted
the projects of the Department, particularly reduction in investment in Public Sector Undertakings and
Aid to autonomous Institutions by the Department. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the
Ministry of Finance should consider the proposal for increase in outlay at RE stage favourably particularly
under R&D Sector , fuel imports, Grant-in-aid salaries and loans. (Para 9.9)
Action Taken
The recommendation of the Committee has been brought to the notice of Ministry of Finance for
their kind consideration.
Comments
The Committee while taking note of the reply would like the Department to pursue the
matter with the Ministry of Finance.

5
Recommendation
The Committee is also of the view that budgetary cut under Industries and Minerals Sector seems
to be based on the really poor performance of the Department in the previous year as the Nuclear Recycle
Board, Heavy Water Board and BRIT failed to utilise approximately 80% of the budget till January, 2017
and in DAE (Projects) scheme the Department failed to utilise any fund at all. The Committee, therefore,
recommends the Department to maximise utilisation of funds in this sector so that Ministry of Finance
does not have to reduce the funds. (Para 9.10)
Action Taken
The recommendation of the Honourable Committee has been brought to the notice of Heads of
Constituent Units in the Department for meticulous planning and reporting through D.O. letter dated
18.05.2017 for timely implementation and monitoring.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply and would like to be apprised of performance of
these programmes during the examination of Demands for Grants 2018-19 by the Committee.
REGULATORY AUTHORITY
Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB)
Recommendation
On the issue of registration of X-ray machines the Committee takes note of easing of application
process and issuance of regulatory consents through e-LORA systems. The Committee also appreciates the
fact that number of X-rays units under the regulatory purview of Atomic Energy Regulatory Board
increased from 5000 in 2013 to 46,173 by October , 2016. (Para 10.15)
Action Taken
The Department accepts the observations of the Honourable Committee regarding issuance of
regulatory consents through e-LORA systems and the increase in the number of X-rays units under the
regulatory purview October, 2016.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation
The Committee also takes note of the efforts made by the Board for ensuring maximum safety of
nuclear reactors. However, the Committee is not happy with the poor fund utilisation under Plan Head
meant for construction of Regional offices at Kolkata and Chennai. The Committee strongly recommends
that construction of regional offices and human resources recruitment to strengthen the regulation must
be completed as per the schedule. (Para 10.16)

6
Action Taken
Construction of regional offices at Kolkata and Chennai is in progress. Around 30% construction
work has been completed at Kolkata and construction has just commenced at Chennai. Rigorous follow
up is being done by AERB for speeding up construction process.
Out of 115 posts of Scientific and Technical posts sanctioned in the XII Plan Project, 5 posts of
SO/C are filled. 12 TSOs allotted to AERB will be joining as SO/C in August, 2017.
Proposal for recruiting M. Tech. students from IIT Bombay and IIT Madras has been initiated.
Advertisement has been published for filling up the posts through lateral transfer from DAE units. The
scrutiny of applications is in progress. Recruitment action for the remaining posts is in active process
and it is expected to be completed soon.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply and would like to be apprised of the progress
achieved on above counts during examination of Demands for Grants 2018-19 of the Department
by the Committee.
VERIABLE ENERGY CYCLOTRON CENTRE (VECC)
Recommendation
The Committee takes note of contribution made by the Variable Energy Cyclotron Centre in international
scientific collaboration such as Large Hadron Collider Grid, European Organisation for Nuclear Research
and ALICE Programme. The Committee commends the role of VECC which is providing assistance to
people of North Eastern States in the field of nuclear medicine facilities especially facilities for
Radioimmunoassay (RIA) tests, operation of Cancer of thyroid patients. The Committee recommends that
facilities for treatment of Thyroid Cancer patients of the North-East region be further expanded to other
areas also.
The Committee also recommends that VECC should be allocated adequate resources so that its
contribution to socially useful applications and the frontier science experiments can be further scaled up.
(Para 12.8 and 12.9)
Action Taken
DAE has been setting up a new Radiation Medicine Research Centre (RMRC) at Rajarhat-Kolkata
campus of VECC and this facility will serve the cancer patients of the country in a much larger way
in future.
The expenditure of VECC under plan budget for the year 2016-17 was ` 63.67 crore. It is to be
noted that the BE for the current year 2017-18 has been allocated ` 73.5 crore. Therefore, the contributions
to socially useful applications and the frontier science experiments can be further scaled up with the
enhanced allocation.

7
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply.
BHABHA ATOMIC RESEARCH CENTRE
Recommendation
The Committee congratulates the Department for its contribution to national security, health and
nutritional security of the country. The Committee also takes notes of setting up of 21 metre diametre
gamma ray telescope being installed at Hanle, Ladakh for high altitude research and development of
Super Computer 'ANUP AM Aganya'. The Committee is hopeful that BARC will keep on contributing to
nation's security in every possible manner and recommends that adequate budgetary provisions should be
made for this purpose. The Committee also hopes that concrete action Plan will be prepared to accomplish
the physical and financial targets set for the year 2017-18. (Para 13.13)
Action Taken
MACE Telescope Hanle, Ladakh
Physical targets and likely completion time-lines:
(1) Installation of MACE mechanical structure at Hanle (completion by July, 2017)
(2) Installation of imaging camera at focal plane (completion by July, 2017)
(3) Testing of camera integrated modules (completion by November, 2017)
(4) Mounting and alignment of 100 mirror panels on the telescope basket (completion by
October, 2017)
(5) Preliminary pointing/tracking runs with some mirror panels (September, 2017)
(6) Functionality testing trial runs (November, 2017)
(7) Start of trial observation runs (January, 2018)
(8) Installation of all 356 mirror panels (July, 2018)
(9) Commissioning of fully configured telescope (August, 2018)
(10) Regular observation of gamma-ray sources with the MACE telescope (September, 2018)
Adequate budgetary provision has been made in BE-16-17.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
NEW CENTRE OF  BHABHA  ATOMIC RSEARCH CENTRE
Recommendation
The Committee finds that progress of new campus of BARC at Visakhapatnam has been tardy. In
past ten years of its existence not much development has taken place. The Department needs to show

8
unflinching commitment and firm resolve to ensure that the construction of the new campus is completed
without any further delay. (Para 14.3)
Action Taken
BARC Campus Visakhapatnam
Construction of the new campus in already acquired land is in full swing. Total 10 numbers of
works are presently in progress for Technical Laboratory buildings and Utility Centres, and are expected
to be completed by March, 2020. The works pertaining to approach road to campus, Guest House and
residential colony are in the final stage of completion and expected to be completed on or before March,
2018. Tender action has already been initiated for balance few more leftover works. All the buildings of
the sanctioned project are expected to be completed by March, 2020.
Slow progress is mainly because of hindrances caused by local villagers during land acquisition
process which are beyond the control of BARC(V). Follow up with APIIC to hand over the balance 1580
acres of land is in progress with the concerned Andhra Pradesh Government authorities.
Comments
The Committee while taking note of the reply hopes that Visakhapatnam campus of BARC
will be completed as per the schedule.
THE GURUSHIKHAR OBSERV ATORY FOR ASTROPHYSICAL SCIENCES (GOALS)
Recommendation
The Committee feels that these issues must be taken up with the Ministries of Urban Development
and Environment, Forest and Climate Change by the Department to make sure that in the interest of
scientific observation, GOALS Observatory is allowed to perform its duties properly. (Para  15.11)
The Committee feels that such a valuable observatory dedicated to the cause of astrophysical
sciences and capable of making the country proud of its achievements, fully deserves all necessary
assistance from the Department. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department of Atomic
Energy must render all the help required by the Gurushikhar Observatory for Astrophysical Sciences
(GOALS) of Bhabha Atomic Research Centre. It also recommends that efforts should not only be made
to meet its requirements after MACE telescope is fully functional but attempts should also be made to
grant expeditious sanction for providing more facilities, so that, the Observatory could be able to excel
further in pursuit of its objectives. (Para 15.12)
Action Taken
Status of GOALS, Mount Abu
The TACTIC (TeV Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescope with Imaging Camera) is operational at
GOALS (Gurushikhar Observatory for Astrophysical Sciences), Mount. Abu (24.60 N, 72.70 E, 1300m
above sea level) for more than fifteen years. The telescope is based on the imaging atmospheric
Cherenkov technique and is used to record images of extremely short duration atmospheric Cherenkov

9
flashes during clear and moonless nights. TACTIC deploys a large light collector and a 349-pixel imaging
camera based on Photo Multiplier Tubes (PMTs).
During 2016-17, we have used TACTIC to observe various galactic and extra-galactic very high
energy (VHE) gamma-ray sources namely Crab Nebula, Markarian 421, Markarian 510, 1ES1215+305,
1ES2344+514 and NGC1275. A total of around 425 hours of data has been recorded during this period.
Comments
The Committee notes that the Department has not furnished any response to the observations/
recommendations in the above paras and would appreciate an affirmative commitment by the
Department in the Action Taken Note.
C-INDUSTRIES AND MINERALS SECTOR
Indian Rare Earths Ltd. (IREL)
Recommendation
Rare Earths are important resources for use in high-tech applications in various strategic sectors
such as defence, atomic energy, space, oil, green energy and electronics, etc. The Committee is of the
view that it is high time that strategies should be adopted to achieve self-reliance in critical strategic
resources like Rare Earths and in the light of its importance, develop a roadmap for exploration and
sustainable mining of rare earth minerals. The Department should also explore measures for encouraging
private sector investment in mining, extraction and manufacturing rare earth based end products.
(Para 17.8)
Action Taken
The beach sand mineral sector has already been opened for private participation from the year 1998
having one of the major objectives of setting up value added industry to meet the requirement of domestic
market.
Aligning further with such objectives, IREL has envisaged setting up of a rare earth based theme
park which would inter alia include demonstration of home-grown technologies from BARC in the field,
skill development centre and state-of-the art laboratory to analyze the raw materials and finished products.
Entrepreneurs will be invited to set up RE based products value chain industries by up scaling the pilot
plant technologies to commercial scale.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
D. MEGA SCIENCES
Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory (LIGO) Facility
Recommendation
The Committee is happy to note that India has been selected as the host country of only third LIGO
facility in the world. Indian scientists must take up this opportunity and utilise the goodwill and

10
advantage. The Committee hopes that India will take advantage of LIGO facility and become a force
to reckon with in study of gravitational waves. (Para No. 18.4)
Action Taken
The Department accepts the observations of the Honourable Committee. The DAE shall facilitate
the Indian Scientists to take up this opportunity and utilise the goodwill and advantage of being a host
country.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
INDIA  AND CERN (EUROPEAN ORGANISATION FOR NUCLEAR RESEARCH)
Recommendation
The Committee is happy to note that India has become an associate Member of the European
Organisation for Nuclear Research (CERN). The Committee hopes that this would prove to be a firm step
in international scientific collaboration and also help in employing human resource from India and
broader participation in the scientific experiments. The Committee feels that Indian Industry must tap
this opportunity for its advantage. (Para No. 19.4)
Action Taken
The Department accepts the observations of the Honourable Committee of India becoming one of
the Associate Members of European Organisation for Nuclear Research (CERN). The Department shall
take it up further to optimise the opportunity available to its advantage to Indian Industry and in
International scientific collaboration by developing human resource from India.
Comments
The Committee, while noting the reply, would like to be apprised about future collaborations
with the Indian industry and international scientific community.
E- HEALTH SECTOR
Tata Memorial Centre (TMC)
Recommendation
The Committee is happy to know about operationalisation of Cancer Hospital at Sangrur in Punjab
and notes the progress made in setting up of Cancer hospital in Vizag, Andhra Pradesh and Mohali,
Punjab. The Committee hopes that these Hospitals will be operationalised as per the schedule.
(Para 20.7)
Action Taken
The observation of the Honourable Committee has been taken note of All efforts will be put in to
ensure that the Cancer Centres in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh and Mohali, Punjab will be commissioned
at the earliest.

11
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation
The Committee commends the Department for setting up a new Cancer Centre in Varanasi, Uttar
Pradesh and hopes that this Centre will cater to the needs of Cancer patients of Northern India
particularly the cities of Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and other States located along the Ganges.
(Para 20.9)
Action Taken
The observation of the Honourable Committee has been taken note of. All efforts will be made to
ensure that the Cancer Centres in Varanasi, U.P. will be commissioned as per schedule.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply.
F- UTILISATION OF NON POWER APPLICATIONS AND SPIN-OFF TECHNOLOGIES FOR
SOCIETAL  AND  INDUSTRIAL  BENEFITS  DEVELOPED  BY  DAE
Recommendation
The Committee appreciates Non-Power Applications and spin-off technologies developed by
Department of Atomic Energy for societal and industrial benefits in the field of agriculture, food
preservation, healthcare and industry, waste disposal and education, etc. It also appreciates development
of Mounisara software for the betterment of quality of life of the citizens of India. In fact, technologies
like Nisargruna can prove to be boon for the society at large and industry which is grappling with the
problem of disposal of sewage as well as solid waste generated in metropolitan cities and small towns.
(Para No. 21.4)
Action Taken
The Department accepts the observations of the Honourable Committee regarding the technologies
developed by the Department for societal and industrial benefits in the field of agriculture, food preservation,
healthcare and industry, waste disposal and education, etc.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation
The Committee commends the Department for starting the seed production programme at Vizag
campus also and hopes that these efforts will benefit Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, North-Eastern States and
generate good quality seeds in eastern India. (Para 21.5)
Action Taken
Currently breeder seed production of pigeon pea and black gram is going on at Vizag in about 5
acres of land. About 20 acres of land of the campus is being fenced. Once the fencing is completed,
seed multiplication effort will be intensified and expanded to 20 acres.

12
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendations
While noting the development of Non-Power Applications and socially useful technologies, the
Committee is concerned with the slow pace at which these non-power applications and socially useful
technologies developed by the Department are trickling down to the targeted groups in particular and
society in general. This is primarily because Scientific Departments have not made any proactive combined
effort to create a dedicated agency and portal for popularisation of socially useful technologies and
other technologies ready for commercialisation. However, DAE has made some good moves in this
direction with Board of Radiation and Isotope Technology. The Committee is aware the DAE has tied
up with a private company, CSIR tech for marketing of socially and industrially useful technology
developed by the Department. (Para 21.6)
The Committee feels that the efficacy of non-power applications and spin-off technologies lies in
their use on a large scale which requires propagation and popularisation of these technologies.
(Para 21.10)
In view of the above, the Committee recommends the Department and BARC to execute their
strategy to aggressively market its non-power applications and socially beneficial technologies such as
Nisargruna Biogas Plant for handling biodegradable wastes, Sludge Hygienization Research Irradiation,
Gamma radiation processing Plan, including its technology on food preservation, molecular medicine
and healthcare, through Board for Technology Transfer and Collaboration Division and other possible
mechanisms so that more and more people get benefitted. AKRUTI Programme of the Department should
also spread its activities outside Maharashtra. (Para 21.11)
Action Taken
Sludge Hygienization, Research Irradiation and Gamma radiation processing Plant
(1) The 100 tons/day sludge hygienisation facility coming up in Ahmedabad is expected to be
operational by September, 2017.
(2) Plant machinery installation has commenced.
(3) Draft MoU has been sent in April, 2017 to Municipal Corporation of Surat for signature and
awaiting their response.
(4) For wider awareness, the discussions and presentations were made in various meetings including
the Journalist meeting and State science councillors meeting recently organized by the
Department in collaborations with NGOs.
Nisargruna Biogas Plant for handling biodegradable wastes
(1) A NISARGRUNA plant with 15 MT/day capacity has been commissioned at the Deonar
abattoir, Mumbai.

13
(2) A NISARGRUNA plant with 10 MT/day capacity has been commissioned at Chennai Municipality,
Chennai.
(3) A NISARGRUNA plant with 5 MT/day capacity has been commissioned to specifically handle
cow dung from gaushala at the municipal workshop, Rajkot, Gujarat.
(4) A NISARGRUNA plant with 250 kg/day capacity has been commissioned at Chikabbalapur,
Bangalore through DAE Technologies Display and Dissemination Facility (DTDDF).
(5) Installation of a NISARGRUNA plant with 0.5 MT/day capacity has been taken up at the H.
N. Bahuguna Garwal University through DTDDF.
(6) BARC is in discussion with municipal corporations in States such as Gujarat, Tamil Nadu,
Puducherry, Sikkim, Chhattisgarh, Rajasthan etc. for dissemination of this technology.
Molecular Medicine and Healthcare
Two radioprotectors that offer protection against radiation toxicity on experimental rodents have
been developed. Clinical trials of these molecules as adjuvants in radiotherapy are being conducted in
collaboration with two private entrepreneurs.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply.
Recommendation
The Committee notes that the Department in collaboration with CSIR-Tech had signed a Memorandum
of Understanding (MoU) for technology transfer and collaboration. However , as per recent media
reports, CSIR-tech has been closed down recently. The Committee, therefore, is of the view that there is
a crying need for marketing and popularisation of socially useful technology developed by various
scientific departments at one platform. (Para 21.12)
Action Taken
Memoranda of Understanding have been signed with several agriculture universities, whereby the
universities are required to test and promote crop varieties developed by BARC.
They are also encouraged to adopt NISARGRUNA technology for treatment of biodegradable
wastes generated in-house and popularize food preservation technologies of BARC amongst user agencies.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation
Food preservation technology developed by BARC known as Trombay crop varieties needs to be
popularised in the States where they are currently not cultivated. The Department should take its
technologies to the people through actively engaging State Governments and other Central Ministries/

14
Departments. The Committee is also of the view that the Department should pull up its socks and get
ready to reap the benefits once the use of fumigants at international level is stopped.
Action Taken
(1) BARC-DAE and State Horticulture Mission (SHM), Bihar have entered into an MoU on 29th
May 2017 for "Promotion and large scale deployment of BARC-DAE Litchi preservation
technology in Bihar". SHM has also shown interest to set up irradiation facility at the surrounding
area of Patna.
(2) For popularization of irradiated foods and deployment of radiation processing technology on
a wider commercial scale, the benefits of radiation processing was conveyed to consumer
groups as well as food industries during various consumer awareness programs. Attempts are
also made to enhance visibility of irradiated food products in the market through their sale at
various retail outlets and super markets.
(3) The Department is interacting with National Institute of Plant Health Management (NIPHM),
Government of India, Hyderabad to enter into collaboration for using the food irradiation
technology as a viable and safe alternative to chemical fumigants for disinfestations of different
food grains and spices.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
NUCLEAR POWER CORPORATION OF INDIA LIMITED
Recommendation
The Committee is happy to note that second unit of Kudankulam attained criticality and synchronised
with grid. The Committee also observes that the future plan of the Department for capacity addition
reveals that 6 indigenous and 5 new reactors with foreign co-operation have been proposed. The Committee
desires that NPCIL should expedite the negotiation process with foreign collaborators in order to achieve
total installed capacity of about 600 MWe by 2024. (Para 23.8)
Action Taken
The second unit of Kudankulam (KKNPP 2 - 1000 MW) which had been synchronised with the
grid on August 29, 2016 commenced commercial operation on March 31, 2017.
NPCIL is making progress on the projects under construction and new projects accorded financial
sanction comprising of six indigenous 700 MW Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors (PHWR) and two
1000 MW Light Water Reactors (LWR) with foreign cooperation. On their progressive completion, the
total installed nuclear power capacity is expected to reach 13480 MW (including 500 MW PFBR being
implemented by BHAVINI) by 2024.
The discussions with foreign partners on various techno-commercial aspects are aimed at arriving
at viable project proposals for setting up nuclear power Plants. The techno-commercial discussions with

15
the foreign partners for setting up nuclear power plants involve many complex issues and their resolution
takes time. However, NPCIL notes the committee's recommendation and will make all efforts to expedite
the discussions and arrive at viable project proposals.
Comments
The Committee while noting the reply would like to be apprised about the progress made
by NPCIL in power generation during Demands for Grants 2018-19 of the Department.
BHARTIYA NABHIKIYA VIDYUT NIGAM LTD. (BHA VINI)
Recommendation
The Committee feels that BHAVINI has an important role to play in bringing energy security to the
country. The Committee is of the view that if India has to successfully realise the three stage Nuclear
Energy Programme and thereby tap huge thorium reserves of the country, Department has to make all
out efforts for expediting the commissioning and ramp up the capacity of Fast Breeder Reactor.
(Para 24.11)
Action Taken
The recommendation of the Honourable Committee is noted.
The Committee observes that there has been inordinate delay in commissioning of Prototype Fast
Breeder Reactor at Kalpakkam. As per the original schedule, the project was to be commissioned in
September, 2010 which was later rescheduled to September, 2014. The goalpost was again shifted to
September, 2016 and later on to October, 2017. The Committee is disappointed to note that despite a
Steering Committee headed by the Secretary himself conducting regular meetings for monitoring the
activities of PFBR, such meetings have not yielded any concrete results as the completion schedule has
been delayed considerably due to various constraints resulting in delay in achieving criticality. While
appreciating the complexities involved in the project and extreme caution exercised by the Department,
the Committee hopes that the Department will expedite the remaining work so that the reactor is
commissioned by October, 2017 without any further delay. (Para 24.12)
Action Taken
The recommendation of the honourable Committee is noted. Presently, all construction activities and
total equipment erection and installation have been completed in Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR).
A number of mandatory pre-requisites tests viz. Integrated Leak Rate Test of Reactor Containment
Building, commissioning of handling flasks for demonstrating the maintainability of Primary Sodium
Pumps, Pressure hold test of Reactor Assembly and Main Vessel and integrated pre-heading of sodium
lines have been completed.
Preparatory jobs are in progress to test the Reactivity control mechanism and Fuel handling equipments
in high temperature environment in Reactor Assembly.

16
Presently, purification of secondary sodium is completed and filling of Secondary sodium main circuit
is in progress. This will be followed by sodium filling in main vessel and loading of fuel sub-assemblies
towards approach to first criticality of the reactor by October 2017.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and recommends that there should be no let up in the
efforts of the Department to ensure timely completion of the first-of-its kind Fast Breeder
Reactor.
OUTREACH  PROGRAMME
Recommendation
The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department and its Public Sector Units such as
Uranium Corporation of India Limited, and Indian Rare Earths Limited should prepare a comprehensive
outreach programme with a calendar of events using social media platforms, radio, television, etc. meant
for students and general public and most importantly for all the elected representatives right from district
level i.e. Members of Zila Panchayats, Legislative Assemblies and Councils and Members of Parliament.
(Para 25.2)
The Committee is aware that some steps in this direction have already been taken by the Department.
Setting up of Hall of Nuclear Energy is one such small step in this direction. The Committee is also aware
of public awareness campaigns done by NPCIL in and around its nuclear reactors. However, it still
believes that a lot more needs to be done for management of unfounded fears among the people and
negative perception against possible adverse fallouts of nuclear energy. (Para 25.3)
The Committee strongly feels that elected representatives can play an important role in making their
constituents aware of non-power applications and spin-off technologies developed by the Department and
its Public Sector Units which have the potential to serve the society in numerous ways and ultimately
create a positive image about nuclear energy in the mind of Indian public at large. (Para 25.4)
Action Taken
The need for Public Awareness on Atomic Energy has been realized since inception of the Department
of Atomic Energy (DAE) and since then it has a dedicated wing for public awareness, the Public
Awareness Division (erstwhile Publicity Division).
2. DAE has been continuously promoting awareness about the peaceful uses of atomic energy
(as in power production, applications of radiation technology in the areas of healthcare, food
and agriculture, industry, water, environment etc.) with prime focus on benefits to the society
and also keeping the public abreast with current trends and developments in the field.
3. In view of the expanding programmes of DAE, and technological advent and digital India, an
urgent need was felt to enhance the scope and quantum of public awareness activities further
by setting up a project called Societal Outreach Program Cell (SOPC) in the Department of
Atomic Energy. SOPC is mandated to spread awareness on the benefits flowing out to the
society from the programmes of the Department by using Social Media Tools.

17
4. DAE has organized and participated in 60 exhibitions in different regions of the country; 36
seminars/workshops for students, academia, general/rural public, members of the media and
NGOs have been conducted; made over 06 video films and multimedia presentation. Recently
DAE has organized a work shop for the benefit of Journalists at BARC from various newspapers/
Electronic Media and also a guided tour to the Tarapur Atomic Power Station.
5. DAE organizes the All India Essay Contest in Nuclear Science and Technology (started during
the Birth Centenary year of Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru) every year. It brought out several
publications on peaceful uses of atomic energy during the last 3 years. Most of the publications
have been done in various local Languages wherever relevant.
6. Various activities to improve and augment visibility of such programmes among general public
are being carried out by the Societal Outreach Programme Cell (SOPC) of DAE. These include
outreach via different media like television, print media, social and digital media, conduct of
workshops, etc. DAE chalked out various Public Outreach programmes for the benefit of
stake holders across the country.
7. As a part of DAE's public outreach activity, a studio interaction / interview of Dr. Sekhar Basu,
Secretary, DAE on Doordarshan has been produced, which has been broadcasted on Doordarshan
National channel and Lok Sabha TV . This studio interaction touches upon different domains
of nuclear energy including the Indian energy scenario, societal and spin-off technologies of
DAE, human resource development and future plans etc. and it also includes a question-
answer session of Secretary, DAE with mass media students.
8. Further, two page advertorials of DAE have been released in "Shubh Yatra" - the in-flight
magazine of Air India and in "Rail Bandhu" - the on-board magazine of Indian Railways, which
are impactful print media options aimed at passengers of Air India and the Indian Railways.
The campaign was received positively among a wide cross-section of passengers including
Government officials, dignitaries like Hon'ble Members of Parliament, State Legislative Assemblies
and other political figures and members of civil society.
9. In addition, DAE's advertisement campaigns were carried out on Lok Sabha Television (LSTV)
during the Parliament Sessions over a period of three months during January 2017 to March
2017, which are quite popular among the parliamentarians and has a large viewership across
the country, especially during the Parliament Sessions. In order to create a positive image
about nuclear energy in the minds of elected representatives, it is further planned to have site
visits for them.
10. Enhanced use of social media is an important activity of the Societal Outreach Programme Cell
(SOPC) of DAE. As a part of this, DAE had launched its official Facebook page at
www.facebook.com/dae.connect. Recently, DAE has also augmented its presence on social
media by launching its Twitter handle @DAEIndia.

18
11. It is the endeavor of DAE to reach out to the teeming millions of people of the country with
the objective of removing misconceptions about atomic energy which is of tremendous importance
and relevance in today's scenario. It is envisaged that systematic implementation of all the
activities by the Public Awareness Division and Societal Outreach Programme Cell (SOPC) of
DAE in association with the constituent units, in a proactive and phased manner, will increase
public outreach multi-fold thus achieving the objective of public acceptance of atomic energy
in India.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the Department would continue its endeavours
to benefit the people and the country at large.

19

INTRODUCTION
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and
Technology, Environment and Forests, having been authorised by the Committee to present the Report
on its behalf, present this Three Hundred Eighth Report on Action Taken by the Ministry of Environment,
Forest and Climate Change on the recommendations/observations contained in the Three Hundredth

REPORT

and Climate Change on the recommendations/observations contained in the Three Hundredth Report of
the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and Technology, Environment and
Forests on the Demands for Grants (2017-18) of the Ministry, which was presented to both the Houses

Hundredth Report of the Committee. Action Taken Notes on the recommendations/observations of the
Committee were received from the Ministry on 14th August, 2017.

of the Committee on the action taken by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change are
set out in the subsequent paragraphs:–

NATIONAL COORDINATED PROGRAMME FOR ASSESSMENT OF NON-TIMBER FOREST
PRODUCT RESOURCES
Recommendation
The Committee notes the dismal performance of the scheme since 2008-09. Not even a penny could
be spent in the scheme for the first two financial years inspite of an allocation of ` 50.00 lakhs during
both the financial years. The performance, both physical as well as financial, of the scheme during the
remaining years of the scheme has been equally disappointing. The reply of the Ministry does not indicate
whether the study on ensuring fair returns to primary collectors of Non-Timber Forest Produce granted
to FRI, Dehradun, for which an amount of `16.01 lakhs was incurred in 2011-12 could be completed
or not. After investing eight crucial years and expending approximately ` 65 lakhs, the scheme has been
closed. The Committee is of the view that the Ministry should make a realistic assessment of its schemes
and embark upon them only if the Ministry is convinced of its utility and success in future.
(Para 9.3)
Action Taken
Ministry has Scheme for National Coordinated Programme for Assessment of Non-Timber Forest
Product Resources, which was introduced in the year 2008-09 in the 11th Five Year Plan Period. The
main objective of the scheme was to carry out assessment, monitoring and evaluation studies in the broad
areas of forest trade, production and disposal of NTFP in the country. Forest Research Institute,
Dehradun has completed study namely 'National Study on Commercial Production of Non-timber Forest
Products for ensuring Fair returns to Primary collectors' and has submitted the draft report to Ministry.
The summary of the study along with key findings and recommendations in the report were presented
by the Principal Investigator of the Project, FRI, Dehradun on 14.06.2017. The observations/comments
made during the meeting have been conveyed to Principal Investigator of the Project, FRI, Dehradun to
incorporate in the final report and to submit to the Ministry. The same is awaited. As the Ministry had
not received good research proposal on NTFP and it was not able to fully utilize the amount allocated
in the above scheme, therefore, the allocation in the scheme was reduced gradually and ultimately scheme
has been closed. However, the view of the Committee regarding making the realistic assessment of the
scheme is noted.

7
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the Ministry would make realistic assessment
about its schemes in future.

Recommendation
The Committee is of the view that certain specimens conserved in ZSI are irreplaceable and some
of them have even become extinct in our country. The specimens are our national assets and they should
be conserved befittingly. It is sad and alarming to note that due to resource constraints, the concerned
authorities are unable to preserve the specimen with modern technologies. The Committee recommends
that the entire building of ZSI should be upgraded and modernized in a time bound manner, on a top
priority basis. The rooms/boxes where the specimens are kept should be temperature controlled. The
modernization of the building would also enable the specimens to be displayed in a way so that visitors
could have a good look at them. ZSI is one the country's most valuable resource centers and therefore,
the building and the conservation areas should be modernized in a manner reflecting their importance
and their place in Indian history. The Committee also recommends that adequate budgetary allocation
should be made for the renovation and modernization of the building and the specimen conserving/
preserving areas. (Para 10.7)
Action Taken
An amount of ` 16.65 crore was released vide Ministry order dated 27.02.2015 specifically for the
works in relation to modernization of ZSI. The various activities are in progress. The other capital works
for modernization of ZSI are considered by the Ministry, as and when the proposal is received. The
allocation for the Capital during 2016-17 was `10.00 crore and allocation for 2017-18 is ` 9.09 crore.
ZSI is an attached office of the Ministry and is under Non-Schemes, and additional funds can be
provided at RE stage, keeping in view the progress of the existing works and requirements of the funds,
and after utilization of the funds already granted.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that there would be no let up in projects being
undertaken for modernization of ZSI and adequate funds will be made available for the execution
of these projects.

POLLUTION ABATEMENT
Recommendation
The Committee notes the reasons furnished by Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
for low utilisation of funds under the scheme. At the same time, the Committee is surprised to note that
the Ministry chose not to respond to the Committee's query regarding the reasons for reduction in the
allocation for the scheme at RE stage. The Committee is of the view that high level of pollution across
the county has been engaging the attention of all concerned and abating pollution has become one of
the gravest challenges today. In such a scenario, if funds earmarked for assistance of Abetment of
Pollution remain partially utilised, that speaks volumes about the sincerity and the capabilities of the
concerned agencies. The Committee therefore, recommends that the Ministry of Environment, Forest and
Climate Change should seriously ponder over the reasons for underutilization and also impress upon all
the concerned agencies to ensure that funds earmarked for the scheme are utilized in a time-bound
manner . The Committee had also dwelt upon this issue in its 283rd Report on Demands for Grants 2016-
17 of the Ministry and would also like to reiterate the recommendation made therein, which is reproduced
below:
"At a time when the Ministry is required to address the grave and critical challenge of deteriorating
air and water quality and increasing noise pollution, the Ministry has not been able to fully utilise
the allocations made for a scheme providing assistance for abatement of pollution. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that the Ministry should take a serious note of its performance under this
scheme and take all necessary measures to ensure that the targets under the scheme are achieved
in future and funds allocated are optimally utilised". (Para 13.7)
Action Taken
The reasons for underutilization under the pollution abatement scheme are as under: (1) Non receipt
of competitive proposals meeting criteria for funding under the scheme; (2) Duplication of schemes in

12
other Ministries; (3) Funding under the scheme was not attractive for the investors; (4) Non-receipt of
utilization from State organizations and State boards. During 2016-17 the scheme was under restructuring
and the focus was on completion of ongoing projects which could not be funded due to non-receipt of
complete documents and Utilization Certificates and the previous releases. The cumulative impact resulted
in less than 50% expenditure resulting in the reduction of RE 2016-17.
Ministry and Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) a Statutory Regulatory Body under the Ministry
have taken a number of steps to deal with the challenges of environmental pollution in a holistic manner.
The steps taken are :–
1. The Government has laid down national Ambient Air Quality standards and has notified
115 emission/effluent standards for 104 different sectors of industries besides 32 general
standards for ambient air, noise and water discharge.
2. Directions have been issued for effective management of solid waste and municipal sewage
to 184 towns.
3. CPCB has issued a comprehensive set of directions under Section 18 (1) (b) of Air (Prevention
and control of Pollution) Act, 1986 for implementation of 42 measures to mitigate air pollution
in major cities.
4. CPCB in association with State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs)/Pollution Control Committees
(PCCs) is monitoring air, noise and water quality across the country under National Ambient
Noise Programme (NANP) and National Water Quality Monitoring Programme (NWMP).
5. Directions have been issued for installation of online (24x7) monitoring devices, adoption of
water conservation practices, etc.
6. Categorization of industrial sectors has been revised under Red, Orange, Green or White
categories based on the concept of pollution index which is a function of emission, effluent,
hazardous waste generated and consumption of resources.
In order to address the issues of underutilization under the scheme, the scheme has been reviewed
and accordingly revamped by merger of schemes namely Assistance for Abatement of Pollution, CETP
and Clean Technology (CT) scheme into single scheme of pollution abatement i.e. 'The new proposed
scheme of pollution abatement.' The new proposed scheme now also lays emphasis on awareness,
capacity building activities, demonstration projects for upcoming technologies, result oriented and time
bound R&D studies for control and abatement of Pollution.
Comments
The Committee notes that reply of the Ministry and hopes that the steps taken would help
address the challenges of environmental pollution in a holistic manner. The Ministry should also
focus on initiating necessary steps to avoid underutilisation of funds.

CHIRU GOAT (TIBETAN ANTELOPE)
Recommendation
The Committee feels that Jammu and Kashmir has been the conflict region for long and many
women there are unable to leave their homes and go out for livelihood. The shawl walas who live there
have been accused of killing the chiru goat in order to procure the wool for making a shahtoosh shawl.
However, the shawl makers say that they do not kill the goats because if they kill a goat for every shawl,
where will the shawls be produced from. The Committee understands that China and Mongolia are
breeding the chiru goats and Mongolia is known for its finest wool. The Committee feels that livelihood
opportunities are very low for the people of Jammu and Kashmir because of the extreme climatic
conditions there and shawl making contributes a lot towards sustainable livelihoods of these people. The
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change should
conserve and breed the chiru goat and vast tract of land should be utilized for conserving the chiru
goats. These goats can then be given to the shawl makers for collecting hair. This would not only increase
the number of these goats but would also add to the sustainable livelihood opportunities of the people
of Jammu and Kashmir, who are a lot dependant on the handicraft of embroidered shawls.    (Para 15.2)

14
Action Taken
Chiru have long been hunted for their underfur - shahtoosh, which is renowned for its quality and
has traditionally been transported to Srinagar, where it is woven into an extremely fine fabric used to
make shawls. However, it takes 3-5 hides to make a single shawl, and the wool cannot be sheared or
combed, so to collect the fur the animals have to be killed.
It is assessed as ‘Near Threatened’  by IUCN (2017), because the current status can only be
maintained with continued high levels of protection in its natural range and strict controls on trade and
manufacture of the shawls made from its underfur: any relaxation in the protection regime are predicted
to result in a rapid population decline due to commercial poaching at a rate meeting the threshold for
a threatened category.
There have been representations from weavers/traders in J and K for the removal of ban on trade
in shatoosh through amendments in the Wildlife Acts of India, J and K State, China, and the CITES in
order to benefit the Shatoosh weaving industry in Kashmir. The feasibility of farming the Chiru or
Tibetan Antelope (Pantholops hodgsonii) for its wool was proposed as an alternative to protect already
depleted wild populations of this species.
Chiru inhabits high altitude Tibetan Plateau and requires large expanse of land for its movement and
ranging patterns to fulfil its feeding and breeding requirements and therefore rearing in captivity is
extremely difficult. The quality of wool depends on the cold and harsh climatic factors operating at high
altitudes (3,800m up to 5,500m) where this animal occurs in nature. It therefore, may not serve the
purpose, if it is kept in captivity below this altitude. As per unconfirmed reports, the Chinese failed to
keep Chiru in captivity due to its poor survival rates. Any attempt to do conservation breeding of Chiru
at very high altitude regions of Ladakh (> 3800m) may neither be economical nor feasible as humans
cannot be posted there continuously for more than 2-3 months to manage the resources due to high rate
of casualties. Prior to the assessment of the technical feasibility and economic viability of captive rearing
or farming of Chiru by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, the issues dealing with
the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 will have to be examined first as Chiru is listed under Schedule-I.
Captive rearing of Chiru or Tibetan antelope will neither serve the purpose of conservation nor can
provide raw material for weavers as these animals cannot be bred in captivity and animals have to be
killed to collect their wool to make the shawls.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.

Recommendation
The Committee notes that the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change is in the process
of framing rules in consultation with the State Governments and concerned stakeholders for the utilisation
of the CAMPA Funds. The Committee is perturbed to note the reports emanating from various quarters

15
that the CAMP A funds are being utilized for purposes other than they are intended for. The Committee

LEAPFROGGING FROM BS-IV TO BS-VI STANDARDS OF EMISSION FOR FUEL VEHICLES
Recommendation
Vehicles are the largest single source of air pollution in most urban areas of the country. Air
pollution from motor vehicles is not only emitted directly into the atmosphere but also from chemical
reactions between pollutants after they have been released into the air. The Committee notes the initiatives
taken by the Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change on leapfrogging from BS-IV to Bharat
Stage-VI norms. The Committee recommends that there should be no let up in the efforts of the Ministry
of Environment, Forest & Climate Change relating to leapfrogging to Bharat Stage-VI standards of
emission and fuel for vehicles. The Committee further recommends that the Ministry should also proactively
coordinate and impress upon the other concerned Ministries of the Government of India to make all out
efforts to ensure that the target of implementing the BS-VI standards of emission for fuel and vehicles
by the year 2020 is achieved. (Para 17.2)
Action Taken
Ministry has already initiated actions to achieve target of BS-VI standards of emission and fuel for
vehicles by the year 2020. Some of the initiatives were already submitted to the Committee. Committee's
recommendations have been noted.
Comments
The Committee recommends that there should be no let up in the efforts of the Ministry
in achieving its targets in this direction.

Recommendation
The Committee notes the reasons furnished by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate
Change for reduction in allocation of Project Tiger and Project Elephant at RE stage in 2016-17.
Getting funds at RE stage for projects of national importance and then surrendering the funds on account
of low-expenditure incurred by the concerned State Governments is really disappointing. The Committee

concerned State Governments to proactively plan their Annual Plan of Operations and release the funds

are not reduced. (Para 19.8)
Action Taken
Recommendations of the Committee have been noted for compliance. Ministry is regularly pursuing
submission of Annual Plan of Operation as well as expenditure progress with concerned State Governments.
There is an addition of one more tiger reserve, namely 'Kamlang Tiger Reserve' in State of Arunachal
Pradesh. States have been requested to make proper provisions as per available budget. States have been
advised to optimally utilize budget and this is being monitored in meetings and by Regional Offices of

Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation
Lion is known as the King of the Forest. Today the number of lions in the country has decreased
and the need of the hour is to come forward to protect them and increase their number. The Committee

17
commends the role of the State Government of Gujarat for having taken timely and prompt conservation
efforts whereby the population of Asiatic lion has increased. However, the Committee is also of the view
that the Asiatic lion is still endangered on account of its low population. The Committee is of the view
that already a mechanism is in place for providing statutory support for protecting Tigers and Elephants.
In view of the reducing number of the Lions, the Committee recommends that Ministry of Environment,
Forest and Climate Change must take necessary steps for providing statutory support for strengthening
lion conservation and, on the lines of Project Tiger and Project Elephant, come up with a 'Project Lion'
to protect Lions and their habitat. (Para 19.18)
Action Taken
The population of Elephant and Tiger is spread across the country but same is not in case of Lion.
However sufficient support for conservation of Lion has been provided to States under the Integrated
Development of Wildlife Habitat (IDWH) Scheme since Lion is also one of the species specified for
recovery plan. Due to the efforts made in this scheme number of lions have been increased from 411
in 2010 to 523 in 2015. The evaluation of existing habitats of Lion is undertaken in IDWH Scheme.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
ISSUES RELATING TO GIR FOREST
Recommendation
In view of the above, the Committee strongly recommends to the Ministry of Environment, Forest
and Climate Change not to reduce the guidelines of eco-sensitive zone from existing 10 kms. to proposed
500 meters by the State Government, as it will surely destroy the Lion habitat. The Committee recommends
that there should be uniformity regarding the declaration of Eco-Sensitive Zones around National Parks
and Wildlife Sanctuaries. (Para 20.5)
Action Taken
During the XXI meeting of the Indian Board for Wildlife held on 21st January, 2002, a 'Wildlife
Conservation Strategy-2002' was adopted wherein point no.9 envisaged that "lands falling within 10 Kms
of the boundaries of National Parks and Sanctuaries should be notified as eco-fragile zones under
Section 3 (v) of the Environment (Protection) Act and Rule 5 Sub-rule (viii) and (x) of the Environment
(Protection) Rules".  This was communicated to all State Governments by the Ministry. However, some
of the State Governments had raised concern over applicability of the 10 Kms. range from the Protected
Area boundary and informed that most of the human habitation and other areas including important cities
in these States would come under the purview of eco-sensitive zone and will adversely affect the
development.
Considering the constraints communicated by the States, the proposal was re-examined by the
National Board for Wildlife in its 2nd meeting held on 17th March, 2005 and it was decided that the
‘delineation of eco-sensitive zones would have to be si te specific and relate to regulation, rather than

18
prohibition, of specific activities'. This decision was also communicated to all the State Governments for
compliance vide letter dated 27th May, 2005.
In response, the Government of Gujarat had submitted proposals for declaration of Eco-Sensitive
Zone around Gir National Park, Gir Sanctuary, Matiyala Sanctuary and Paniya Sanctuary to the Ministry.
The draft notification of ESZ around Gir National Park, Gir Sanctuary, Matiyala Sanctuary and Paniya
Sanctuary was issued by the Ministry on 25th October, 2016.
Subsequently, in the 25th Meeting of the ESZ Expert Committee held on 11th April, 2017 in
MoEFCC under the Chairmanship of the Additional Secretary, MoEFCC, the proposal for ESZ around
Gir Landscape was considered and after deliberations, the Committee recommended the proposal for
Final Notification with minimum distance of 500 meter and upto a distance of 9.4 Km. so as to have
minimum adverse affect.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation
The Committee also recommends that Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
and Government of Gujarat should look into the issues brought out above which were raised by the
members of the Civil Society and local representatives during the meeting. Further, the Committee
observes that Gir National Park is very poorly connected by air. The Committee recommends that Union
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and Government should take up the matter with
the concerned Central and State Government agencies so that air connectivity to Gir Forest can be
improved. Further, the Committee is of the view that policy of granting license to dhabas/hotels being
run near the national park needs to be reviewed keeping in view of the fact that lot of garbage is
generated and thrown by these dhabas/hotels etc. in the area. The Committee also recommends that illegal
construction or encroachment in and around the national park should be viewed seriously and stringent
steps must be taken in this direction. (Para 20.6)
Action Taken
Encroachment and construction around the National Parks and Sanctuaries is in purview of States.
In so far as Gir National Park is concerned, State Government of Gujarat has been communicated to
take action according to the recommendations of Committee. Ministry has also taken up the matter with
Ministry of Civil Aviation regarding poor air connectivity of Gir National Park and requested for improving
air connectivity.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply. The Committee is of the view that although encroachment
and construction around National Parks and Sanctuaries is in the purview of the States, the
Ministry can always impress upon the concerned State Governments to comply with the laws in
this regards.

19
Recommendation

has examined the report of the expert Committee threadbare. (Para 20.7)
Action Taken
The proposal of 'Girnar Ropeway' has been approved in 22nd meeting of National Board for Wildlife

Recommendation
The Committee feels that the local people of Kutch deserve appreciation for their contribution in
developing and preserving whole landscape of the Rann of Kutch and congratulates them for their

Ministry has conveyed the appreciation by the Committee for the efforts of local people of Rann

The Committee notes the reply.

The Committee feels that all the issues brought out in the preceding paragraphs deserve attention
and recommends that Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and Government of Gujarat
to consider these issues and take necessary action. The Committee also notes that a large number of
tourists come to visit the Rann of Kutch and leave behind a lot of garbage including plastic wrappers
and bottles that lie scattered in that area. The Committee is of the view that there is a need to ban the

having recharging capacity using local traditional methods, the Committee recommends that the State

PRIV ATE LAND PARTICIPATION IN PRESERV ATION AND CONSERV ATION OF FORESTS
Recommendation
The Committee feels that as the forest cover of the country has been drastically and constantly
depleting, there is a need to involve private sector in increasing the forest cover of the country by
encouraging private land participation in preservation and conservation of forests. There are a lot of
people in the country who are having large landholdings and that they would be happy to contribute to
increasing the forest cover of the country. This would also give a boost to the shrinking forest cover of
the country. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
should consider the suggestions received by the Committee as mentioned above. The Committee also
recommends that the Ministry should consider giving tax exemptions and compensations to those who
proposed to raise forests on the big areas of land available with them. They should be incentivized only
when the land available with them grows as forest, so that the green area cover of the country grows.
This will not only increase India's forest cover, meet some of the Green India Mission requirements but
also bring in much needed private participation in conservation and preservation of forests.
(Para 22.3)

21
Action Taken
The Ministry accepts the recommendations of the Committee as the same would encourage the
people for taking up plantation on private lands owned by them on voluntary basis. It will help in
increasing the green cover of the country and enhancing carbon stock. The suggestions of the Committee
such as Tax exemption, exemption from application of the restriction of Rural Land Ceiling to the private
land have been sent to Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Rural Development for necessary action.
Restriction on area that can be developed (Not exceeding 5% for instance) attracts the provision of
Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 as this would involve land use change.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and would like the Ministry to inform the Committee of the
development in the matter.

INTRODUCTION
Mandate of the Department of Biotechnology (DBT)
1.1 The Department of Biotechnology was set up as an Independent Board in the year 1982, and
thereafter became a full-fledged Department under Ministry of Science & Technology in 1986. The
mandate of the Department is given below:
- To evolve policies and integrated programmes in biotechnology and ensure their implementation
and monitoring.
- To identify specific programmes of Research and Development and manufacturing in biologicals
and biotechnology and oversee the initiation and pursuit of related research and manufacturing
activities.
- To identify, set up and support Centres of Excellence for Research and Development in
biotechnology and ensure proper dovetailing of their activities as per national priorities and
objectives.
- To act as a screening, advising and approving agent of the Government with regard to import
and transfer of new technologies for the manufacture of biologicals, biotechnological products
and their intermediates.
- Evolve safety guidelines for biotechnology Research and Development and manufacturing in
India.
- To act as the central agency for the import of genetically manipulated materials, culture, cells,
specimens, tissues and biotech products including DNA and RNA of any type or size and for
promoting their production in the country.
- Serve as the inter-ministerial and interagency nodal point for all specific international bilateral
and multilateral Research and Development collaborations and agreements in the area of
biotechnology; act as the nodal point for all technology transfers in the area of biotechnology.
- Manufacture and ensure application of recombinant, cell-based and DNA vaccines, diagnostics
and other biotechnological products.
- To evolve programmes for Human Resource Development in the area of biotechnology.
- Serve as an administrative and implementing Department of agencies, commissions, boards,
etc. specifically formed by the Government for fulfilling the national objectives in biotechnology
and also to serve as the nodal point for Bio-informatics including training and creation of
infrastructure, collection, dissemination and exchange of information relating to biotechnology.

INDUSTRY-ACADEMIA COLLABORATIVE MISSION FOR ACCELERATING DISCOVERY RESEARCH

(i) Mission Innovation in Clean Energy:
Mission Innovation (MI) is a global initiative of 22 countries and the European Union to accelerate
global clean energy innovation. MI was announced on 30th November, 2015 in Paris during COP-21.
As part of the initiative, participating countries have committed to seek to double their government's clean
energy research and development (R&D) investments over five years. The second Mission Innovation
Ministerial (MI Ministerial) was held in Beijing China (in June 2016), where leaders of MI countries
announced seven innovation challenges for advancement of clean energy technologies.

The Department of Biotechnology through its programmes on Waste to Energy will Partner with
Ministry of Urban Development and Swachh Bharat Mission to demonstrate technologies at Pilot Scale
for converting Municipal Solid and liquid waste to Energy. The Municipal Corporation and other private
sectors will be involved. These demo plants can be set up in cooperation with the Smart City Projects.
Through competitive process Waste to Energy proposals have been identified for demonstration of
innovative and viable processes over traditional methods like land filling and saving the environment from
adverse effects of global warming by minimizing the emissions of methane from landfill sites. One
demonstration project and 5 R&D projects have been sanctioned during the year. Two demonstration
projects are under consideration. It is expected that the successful technologies can then be transferred
to Municipal Corporations for implementation to disposal off MSW more scientifically and environment
friendly manner.
(iii) Reinventing the Toilets:

integration of proven technologies and known knowledge customized in easily takeaway module for

6. CROP BIOTECHNOLOGY
6.1 The Department has informed the Committee that the mandate of Agriculture Biotechnology program
is knowledge generation, technology and product development for productivity gains, enhanced nutrition
and ensuring quality, resistance to drought salinity, high temperature, resistance to pests and diseases,
input use efficiency, climate resilience and biosafety. The nature and types of programs include product
oriented basic research, translational R&D projects, national networks, autonomous institutions, grand
challenge program, centers of excellence, international collaboration, public-private partnership, etc. It
has been informed that agriculture biotechnology programme deals with a wide range of economically
important crops including rice, wheat, cotton, millets, oilseeds and pulses. Key focus and support areas
are: (i) Nutritional quality & productivity of crops (ii) Climate resilient varietal development in crops
(iii) Biotic stress (iv) trait discovery and marker assisted introgression (v) IT interface technology in

11
agriculture (vi) Big data in agriculture (vii) Sustainable crop development (viii) establishment of technology
platforms. Under major initiatives, during the period 2016-17 and 2017-18, the Department has supported
new projects on improving oil quality and productivity in Groundnut, genome wide association study in
Phaseolus vulgaris - Colletotrichum lindemuthianum  pathosystem, development of genetic stocks for
maturity and growth habit genes in Soybean. Network programs were supported on double haploid
platform for accelerated maize breeding, hybrid development and enhanced genetic gains in South Asia,
marker-assisted breeding and mapping of QTLs for drought tolerance in wheat, genomics-assisted
introgression and field evaluation of rice varieties with genes/QTLs for yield under drought, flood and
salt stress, characterization, race profiling and genetic analysis of wheat powdery mildew pathogen in
India.
6.2 Network programmes on fiber quality traits of cotton, on rust resistance, on biotic and abiotic
stresses in wheat and quality in wheat and on intrigression of abiotic stress traits in rice have been
initiated. 189 ongoing projects and 42 network projects have been supported. Major achievements of the
Department include: A herbicide tolerant mutant of Nagina 22, (named as  Robin) identified, mapped and
characterised earlier is being used in marker assisted backcross breeding program to introgress herbicide
tolerance in 10 varieties of rice viz. PB1121, PB 1509, Sahabhagidhan, Naveen, Pooja Swarna-Sub1, C0
51, Anna, CB 06803 and CB 08702. At Directorate of Wheat Research, Karnal, a project was initiated
for improving biscuit making quality of wheat in North Western Plains using MAS. Prebred PBW373 and
UP2425 lines developed by crossing Nap Hal as source of Glu-D1 double null during 1st phase of the
project were used for Glu-D1 donor as main activity.
6.3 Responding to the query of the Committee about the preparedness of the Department to address
the issues of biotic and abiotic stresses and improving yield and quality traits of the existing crops
through its research activities, the Department has submitted that it is aware of the challenges posed by
the climate change which is the primary contributor to abiotic stresses in crop, evolution of the new
pests and pathogens (biotic stresses). In addition, the Department is also focusing on yield and quality
traits in crops. The Committee was also informed that the Department in order to target these issues
is supporting 56 ongoing projects through extra mural support; 7 projects are on nutritional quality, 19
on yield improvement and 30 on biotic and abiotic stress.
6.4 The Committee appreciates the efforts being undertaken and progress achieved by the
Department in the field of Crop Biotechnology during the year 2016-17 and 2017-18. The Committee
is hopeful that with its earnest efforts in this direction the Department would be able to fetch
the desired results. The Committee, however, feels that the institutional linkage between the
Department and the agricultural universities along with ICAR further needs to be strengthened.
The Committee is also of the view that the Department should collaborate with the International
institutes of repute working in these fields. The Committee, therefore, recommends the
Department to forge partnerships with such institutes to further intensify its research activities
in the field of agricultural biotechnology.
6.5 The Committee also notes that the Department has been supporting a research and
development proposal for development of rust resistant variety in Brassica juncea and a proposal

12
has also been supported for dissecting the molecular interface between the biotrophic pathogen
Sporisorium scitamineum  and its host sugarcane. The Committee, however, feels that drought
resistance varieties of sugarcane, if made available, will ease out the problems, to a considerable
extent, being faced by the sugarcane growers in the country due to lack of irrigation facilities
and dependence on the vagaries of monsoon. The Committee, therefore, recommends the
Department to also start its research and development activities in the direction of developing
